name: Aelea Commodities
summary: The FY2026 earnings recovery is real in the published accounts, but not yet owner cash. Group revenue rose to ₹381.50 crore and PAT to ₹21.32 crore while CFO was −₹30.26 crore and debt including lease principal reached ₹111.60 crore. More importantly, the original FY2025 positive CFO disappears when purchase-invoice financing is correctly presented as borrowing in the FY2026 comparative. BQS 3.06 and Growth Quality 2.60 describe a cash-intensive commodity-processing turnaround, not a proven compounder. IAS is NS: the linked base expansion case has a ₹15.36 crore funding gap even with the identified additional sanction. A funded zero-expansion sensitivity returns 9.81%, below a 15% hurdle, and is not the actual expansion plan. Keep on a cash-conversion watchlist, not an implementation-ready buy list.

sections.title: Executive Verdict

sections.title: Research Header and Gates
sections.text: As of 20 October 2026; BSE SME 544213, ISIN INE0T3401029. Primary IPO/deck evidence places listing on 22 July 2024; the decoded security-master date 13 April 2026 is not treated as original listing. 20,368,800 shares reconcile annual report, August voting denominator and current master. Dated secondary 19 October close ₹136.85 gives equity value ₹278.75 crore and reported FY26 P/E 13.08x. Consolidated Indian GAAP Accounting Standards under Section 133, not Ind AS; three wholly owned subsidiaries, no minority-interest deduction. G1 Integrity: Conditional, without a fraud finding; G2 Reliability: Conditional after the material supplier-financing reclassification is reconciled; G3 Funding: Hold — unresolved for the expansion plan; G4 Tradability: Conditional for a conservative liquidity band, with current BSE surveillance and live execution unverified. Research completeness does not mean every investment gate passes.

sections.title: Canonical Scorecard and Audit
sections.text: GOV 4, MOAT 3, REV 2, DUR 4, CAP 3, CASH 1, BAL 3, EXEC 4 and EARN 3. BQS = 20% GOV+20% MOAT+12% REV+10% DUR+12% CAP+10% CASH+8% BAL+8% EXEC=3.06. Growth Quality = 40% REV+20% DUR+15% EARN+15% CAP+10% CASH=2.60; persistent CAP/CASH weakness invokes the 5 cap, which does not bind this lower result. IAS uses Q 3.06, R NS, D 2, P 3, L 5. Known weighted contribution 1.965, coverage 65%, unrenormalized mathematical range 2.315–5.465; this range is not a target or probability interval. Final IAS NS. Evidence confidence is Medium for scored factors; forecast uncertainty is High. R remains unscored for a substantive expansion/funding gap, not merely unavailable live price data.

sections.title: Business Economics and Industry Position
sections.text: Aelea moved from broad agricultural commodity trading toward raw-cashew-nut processing, kernels and by-products. FY26 manufactured domestic sales ₹362.9671 crore represent about 95.1% of group revenue; traded goods ₹18.2621 crore are much smaller than in earlier periods. This is not automatically volume growth: quality, kernel recovery, commodity price and mix affect invoiced value. In the signed May call management reported around 16,000 tonnes RCN processed in H2 and broadly similar H1, 94–95% utilization and approximately 95% African-origin material procured through merchant intermediaries, not its own established farm-gate entities. Processing scale creates operating leverage but ties up imported/raw-process inventory and bank facilities. The wholesale distributor rather than the end consumer is often the accounting customer.

sections.title: Moat and Competitive Cross-check
sections.text: 140 MTPD mechanized capacity, sourcing expertise and FSSC22000 certification can improve yield, consistency and access. These do not establish durable pricing power. Management put B2C at only about 1% of sales and acknowledged price-per-weight comparisons; premium brand economics therefore cannot be applied to the whole company. African merchant sourcing, competing processors, commodity-price changes and shipping delays constrain margins. Ground-mounted solar and downstream CNSL/cardanol/activated-carbon plans are potential cost/product improvements, not an existing verified moat. No independently established repeat-order retention, customer switching cost, enforceable exclusivity or sustained peer-adjusted excess return was found. MOAT 3 reflects this evidence, not a claim that the business has no processing skill.

sections.title: Revenue History, Scope and Growth
sections.text: Primary comparable group revenue FY21–26 is ₹475.4735/102.7575/108.9474/142.3726/182.1355/381.5041 crore. Five-year CAGR −4.308% is the preselected framework basis, despite three-year 51.854%. Both are disclosed; the changed mix does not justify silently deleting the earlier trading contraction. REV starts 1 and receives only the permitted +1 for two strong FY26 halves, ending 2. The July provisional Q1 update reports revenue/invoicing above ₹108 crore and 81% Q2 capacity booking, explicitly unaudited and unreviewed. Neither is a substitute for H1 FY2026–27 audited/reviewed earnings, collections or bank balances. The prospectus summary has swapped consolidated/standalone labels; detailed signed annexures reconcile to annual group revenue and are used instead. Original FY21 standalone ₹392.13 crore must not be mixed into the group CAGR.

sections.title: Growth Quality and Capital Allocation
sections.text: The ₹21.3152 crore FY26 PAT follows ₹1.1587 crore in FY25 and restated ₹12.2232 crore in FY24, not a smooth exponential trend. FY22 restated profit included a deferred-tax credit; earlier restatements changed depreciation, preoperative costs, gratuity and taxes. Normalizing FY26 by removing ₹0.3098 crore other income at 24–28% tax gives PAT approximately ₹21.08–21.09 crore, so other income alone does not explain the recovery. It still does not convert into cash. Using core EBIT=PBT+finance cost−other income,26% normalized tax and equity+interest-bearing debt, five-year incremental return is roughly 6.1%, versus about 13.7% over the three-year rebound and a much stronger one-year rebound. Capital scopes/restatement/revaluation differences are disclosed and the coarse CAP 3 is robust to modest adjustments. A12–15% capital hurdle is not convincingly cleared over the longer window. New phases must improve cash returns, not just turnover or reported EBITDA.

sections.title: Governance, Ownership and Related Parties
sections.text: The 25 August AGM voting table records promoter/category holdings 12,983,100 of 20,368,800 shares, about 63.74%, at the meeting record date; it is not a 30 September shareholding or current pledge certificate. Annual notes separately list two individual promoters totaling 58.25%, not the whole group. FY26 related-party sales to Sumita A Patel, described as promoter/director-relative and wholesale/retail distributor, are ₹117.686 crore, about 30.85% of group revenue, versus ₹38.7889 crore in FY25. Closing related receivable is shown nil versus ₹2.7284 crore previously. AOC-2 identifies a ₹125 crore ceiling approved 20 August 2025 and calls the transactions arm’s-length. That assertion and a nil closing balance do not independently verify pricing, timing or end-customer sell-through; no round-tripping allegation is made. Executive pay totals about ₹2.039 crore, relative consultancy ₹0.42 crore and connected-foundation CSR ₹0.092 crore. May 2025 land purchase from the same related party lacks consideration in that event filing; prior-year booked land transactions must be reconciled before asserting an omission. Statutory opinion is unmodified; the secretarial report discloses delayed system-driven information submission. The audit-trail paragraph confirms software has an edit-log feature, not an explicit full-year no-tampering certification.

sections.title: Financial History and Forensic Reconciliation
sections.text: All amounts are ₹crore. FY21–26 PAT:11.0851/10.6311/1.9123/12.2232/1.1587/21.3152. Corresponding CFO:−13.5652/+4.8529/+5.0305/−6.5875/−29.1999/−30.2613; capex:12.6989/14.6660/9.0871/1.2102/26.2276/17.5381. The detailed history retains source and scope. Three-year CFO/PAT −1.904; six-year−1.196. Crucially, FY25 original CFO+9.4685 was revised to−29.1999:₹38.1699 crore purchase-invoice financing moved from payables to bank borrowings, and ₹0.4985 crore moved between operating and investing presentation. Financing inflow increases by the same ₹38.1699; net cash stays −₹0.3169. Original FY25 debt ₹11.9463 therefore understates the comparable ₹50.1162 debt. This is a reconciled classification change, not unexplained missing cash. FY26 inventory ₹110.8302 includes ₹103.5622 WIP; AR ₹37.3582 includes ₹4.5 crore older than three years, still reported good without allowance. Government balances ₹10.1843 and vendor advances ₹3.6441 absorb additional cash. Cash ₹6.2115 is kept separate from other bank/deposit balances. The model reserves ₹5.4783 net current-tax liability and ₹2.9042 capital creditors; current finance-lease maturity ₹0.3329 is added to debt, not lost in other liabilities. FCTR ₹2.2386 is added in the published CFO bridge; translation and bank/lease classifications deserve further explanatory disclosure, but removing that add-back only worsens already-negative conversion. No unexplained positive cash benefit is relied upon. Standalone CARO points to note 39: March stock/book-debt balances ₹120.7371 crore in books versus ₹116.80 crore submitted to banks, a ₹3.9371 crore difference. The note attributes book-debt differences to exclusion of related receivables and grossing of customer advances; the component-by-component bridge is not supplied. This is a disclosed reconciliation item, not evidence of fictitious stock or an observed default. CARO reports no borrowing default or reported fraud during FY26.

sections.title: Valuation, Funding Bridge and Scenarios
sections.text: A five-year consolidated model starts from actual cash ₹6.2115, debt ₹111.5951, operating WC ₹158.1642 and 2.03688 crore shares. No FY25 IPO proceeds are added again. Forecast WC ratios apply only to incremental revenue, never backward to opening balances. Base growth 15/12/10/8/6%, EBITDA 10.5%, incremental WC40%, maintenance ₹4 crore escalating 5%, expansion ₹25 crore and 12x terminal normalized NOPAT; bull 30/20/15/12/10%,12% EBITDA,35% WC, ₹45 crore expansion and 15x; bear−25/0/3/5/5%,6% EBITDA and 8x. These are analyst sensitivities, not company guidance. Existing revolving facilities must roll; only the signed June ₹13.86 crore HDFC facility is considered possible incremental funding, tested at full/half/zero availability. ₹150 crore rated facilities include ₹39 crore LC and ₹10.89 crore proposed WC; the ₹350 crore borrowing resolution is not cash. Base and bull peak gaps ₹15.36/₹31.40 crore mean no investable IRR. With no expansion, the base sensitivity funds and returns 9.81% after 1% entry/exit friction and 0.5% annual dilution, below 15% hurdle. Actual phase-II/III remaining cost is unquantified, so this optimistic deferral cannot become R. There are no dividends assumed, no double-counted asset sale proceeds and no rescue equity magically added. Terminal illustrations for unfunded cases are not price targets.

sections.title: Bear Case, Permanent-Loss Paths and Survivability
sections.text: A processing margin squeeze can coincide with inventory valuation losses, delayed collections and withdrawal of short-term supplier/invoice financing. The explicit bear charges 20% inventory,10% receivables/vendor-advance cash impairment,30 extra receivable days and 30% withdrawal of March short-term debt, without crediting automatic inventory release. The resulting peak gap is about ₹130.97 crore with no positive terminal equity under the modeled path. These are stress assumptions, not a prediction of default or a claim about actual bad stock. A BBB/Stable rating and signed sanctions are relevant positives but not a guarantee of renewal or liquidation recovery. Concentrated related distribution and old receivables heighten the need for independently evidenced cash collection. D 2 reflects severe downside under a plausible combined operating/funding shock; no numerical default probability is invented.

sections.title: Fivefold and Tenfold Reality Check
sections.text: Fivefold and tenfold price outcomes would require approximately ₹684/₹1,369 per share before friction. With modeled 0.5% annual dilution, year-five equity values would be roughly ₹1,429/₹2,858 crore, before adding any remaining net debt to reach enterprise value. At12x NOPAT and 26% tax, that implies EBIT above ₹161/₹322 crore even before net debt, versus FY26 core ₹36.42 crore. Current 140 MTPD equipment, already claimed 94–95% utilized, cannot mechanically deliver that through volume alone. Management’s 2037 aspiration for 1000 MTPD and additional nuts/retail businesses has no fully financed cost, return or timing bridge in the evidence reviewed. No 5x/10x label is awarded on TAM or extrapolated PAT recovery.

sections.title: Monitoring and Kill Criteria
sections.text: Require the next H1 FY2026–27 financials to reconcile CFO, inventory/WIP, government recoverables, related-party sales/collections and actual bank draws. Obtain phase-II/III remaining committed cost, approved solar timeline and quantified capacity/yield bridge; distinguish contracted from merely proposed facilities. Verify the 13.86 crore loan’s coupon, amortization, conditions and available balance, rather than assuming full October headroom. Track overdue ₹4.5 crore receivables and cash tax settlement. Recheck current BSE restrictions, lot, executable bid depth and corporate actions before any order. Stop considering an investment if collections fail, inventory losses undermine equity, planned expansion lacks funding, related-party terms cannot be substantiated or audited/reviewed information contradicts the cash bridge. These are monitoring thresholds, not assertions that breaches have occurred.

sections.title: Classification and Liquidity Implementation
sections.text: Classification: low-quality cash-conversion turnaround/watchlist with conditional funding, not a durable high-quality growth compounder. Sixty secondary OHLCV rows cover 24 July–19 October. Low/high price×volume bounds give mean turnover ₹36.18–38.14 lakh/day and median ₹29.75–30.82 lakh. A ₹5 lakh sale at 5% participation needs 3.25–3.36 sessions;2% requires 8.11–8.40 and 10%1.62–1.68. These are historical capacity proxies, not observed cash turnover or promised execution. Current master supports eligible BSE SM,600-share lot worth ₹82,110 and 20% bounds ₹109.50–164.20. L 5 is a conservative conditional band:7 raw, −1 lot granularity, −1 secondary/depth/restriction uncertainty. A secondary May snapshot shows prior ASM exits, not October clearance. Historical actions can recur and exchange flags are not misconduct findings. BQS/GQS are rankable as quality assessments; IAS and implementation are not rankable because R is unresolved.

sections.title: Sources, Confidence and Open Evidence
sections.text: Primary sources include the issuer FY24–26 annual reports, original standalone FY21–23 statements, detailed restated DRHP/final-prospectus annexures, signed May 2026 call transcript and deck, June loan disclosures, July unaudited update, August AGM voting/meeting outcome and October signed rating letter. Official security-master data are decoded using the current NSE MII-format specification. Market OHLCV is secondary and explicitly bounded. The full October CRISIL rationale was inaccessible; the signed letter and facility annexure were read, so no rationale/headroom is invented. Remaining material gaps are actual post-March cash/draws, phase expenditure, current BSE restriction status, independently substantiated related-party pricing/collections, the detailed bank-return bridge and current pledge status. These prevent an unconditional investment verdict but do not erase the supported negative cash history. All score formulas, missingness and model assumptions are retained for audit.

valuation.scope: Consolidated AS. Forward scenarios anchored to FY26 actual balances, with identified June borrowing facility considered once. This is not a verified October balance sheet.

assumptions.working_capital: Actual FY26 operating working capital: inventory 110.8302 + receivables 37.3582 + vendor advances 3.6441 + government balances 10.1843 + employee advance 0.0052 + prepaid expenses 0.2935 + other receivables 0.5643 − trade payables 1.3904 − employee payable 1.9146 − statutory dues 0.2264 − customer advances 1.0663 − expense provision 0.1179, all ₹ crore. Capital creditors, tax and lease principal are excluded and settled separately. No opening ratio backfill. Incremental net working capital is 40/35/45% of positive revenue changes in base/bull/bear; no automatic release is assumed in the bear decline.
assumptions.funding: The signed 23 June HDFC sanction of ₹13.86 crore for a working-capital term loan is the sole possible incremental facility, tested at full/half/zero availability. It is not added as both opening cash and debt. Modeled borrowing cost is 12%, or 15% in bear, compared with disclosed facilities at 8.5–13.5%. Exact ECLGS coupon/amortization is unavailable: 10% annual repayment of new principal from year 2 is a model assumption, not a contractual claim. Existing short-term supplier/invoice financing is assumed to roll, supported but not guaranteed by recent continuing rated facilities. Bear withdraws 30% of March short-term borrowings. No funding credit is given to the ₹150 crore rating headline, ₹39 crore LC, ₹10.89 crore proposed working capital or ₹350 crore borrowing resolution.
assumptions.operations: Five annual steps: base growth 15/12/10/8/6% and EBITDA margin 10.5%; bull 30/20/15/12/10% and 12%; bear −25/0/3/5/5% and 6%. Growth represents price, mix, recovery and limited expansion, not mechanically increasing raw-cashew tonnage above 140 MTPD. Maintenance capex of ₹4 crore grows 5%. Remaining phase-II/III spending is unquantified; ₹25/45 crore expansion assumptions are sensitivity budgets, not verified commitments. No value is assigned to the 1000 MTPD aspiration for 2037.
assumptions.opening_obligations: Only ₹6.2115 crore of March cash is included. Net current tax of ₹5.4783 crore and capital creditors of ₹2.9042 crore are settled in year 1, in addition to forward tax and incremental capex. Expansion budgets are deliberately incremental to unpaid capital creditors. No IPO cash is added because the FY25 issue is already reflected in the balance sheet.
